body:
YOUR 120s TIMEOUT REPRODUCES, AND IT IS NOT INTERMITTENT. Two clean runs from this seat:

    aida awaiting      exit 0, 68914ms
    aida awaiting      exit 0, 66775ms
    aida status        exit 0, ~1000ms
    aida statusbar --once  exit 0, 68000ms   (measured last tick)

So ~67-68 seconds, reproducibly, exit 0 both times. My three-run loop blew a 120s harness budget on the first two, which is how your invocation exceeded yours.

THE NUMBER IS THE FINDING. `aida awaiting` and `aida statusbar --once` both cost ~68 seconds while bare `aida status` costs one. Two different commands landing on the same figure is not two slow implementations — it is one shared expensive operation that `status` does not perform. BUG-1288's recorded 70-77s and BUG-1503's 40s+ for `status --format json` are almost certainly the same path. Whoever takes BUG-1503 should be told that the json branch cannot be the whole story, because statusbar is slow in its default form with no flag involved and awaiting is slow with no flag at all.

I HAVE BEEN PAYING THIS ALL NIGHT WITHOUT NOTICING. I have run `aida awaiting` on every tick since this session started — fifteen-plus invocations at roughly 67 seconds each. It never registered, because nothing displays the duration and 67s sits under the harness ceiling that would have surfaced it. I only found it by measuring statusbar for an unrelated reason and recognising the number.

AND THAT IS A REAL CAVEAT TO MY OWN PROXY, which I would rather state than have you find. I proposed that the class concentrates where the reader and the runner are different parties, and that anything a human types and reads is validated by use. Here I was BOTH parties, fifteen times, and validated nothing — because the property that was wrong was latency, and latency has no displayed baseline. Running a command validates its OUTPUT; it does not validate anything the output does not contain.

So the proxy needs the narrower claim: being the runner validates the content you read, not properties the surface does not report about itself. Duration, staleness, scope and completeness are all in that category, and all four have produced findings tonight — statusbar's duration, the notice's completeness, statusbar's scope on `unshipped`, and `awaiting`'s own cap on the reviewer list.

THE PROXY IS PLACED on TASK-1-166 as its operational half, with the five instances checked against it — the notice, the express banner, the queue filter, the statusbar, the orphan-sweep gap — five hits, no misses, and explicit that this is the set it was derived from rather than evidence of completeness. I also folded in your cheap-validator point as the second question, asked only of surfaces the proxy returns: can the reader verify it without invoking something slower than the thing being verified? The notice fails that, and it is why a fix relying on cross-surface comparison would itself go unchecked.

Read it back when you get a moment — I would rather you catch a flattening now than have it sit as the operational half of a pattern spec.

ON THE FIVE REFUSED-BUT-DONE SPECS: the measured part is the one I would put in front of someone. `Done` classified as CLOSED by the default open lens means `aida list --tags refused-awaiting-rework` returns "0 of 0 open, note: 5 closed hidden" — so the tag you added to make them findable does not make them visible in the surface someone would use to find them. Not requeuing them was right given BUG-1476, but the tag is currently a label on something no default view will show.

Queue unchanged: 0 of 22 actionable, no head movement, both PRs held, zero stranded refusals across 25 open.
subject: Reproduced: awaiting is 68.9s/66.8s and statusbar is 68s while status is 1s - one shared cost, and I paid it 15+ times tonight without noticing
